id: conventions.formats.editorconfig
---
## EditorConfig & line endings
> Load when: creating a repo, or adding `.editorconfig` or `.gitattributes`.

- `.editorconfig` at the repo root with `root = true`.
- `[*]`: `charset = utf-8`, `end_of_line = lf`, `insert_final_newline = true`, `trim_trailing_whitespace = true` (Markdown included: no trailing-space breaks, `CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/STYLE.md`).
- Indent per language: 2 spaces default; tabs for Go and `Makefile`; 4 spaces where the language standard says so (Python).
- `.gitattributes` first line `* text=auto eol=lf`; mark binaries (`*.png binary`).
- Never commit CRLF; Windows editors and WSL checkouts follow these files (`CONVENTIONS/SYSTEMS/WINDOWS-WSL2.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/ENV.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.env
---
## .env files
> Load when: adding a `.env` file, `.env.example`, or env-file loading to a project.

- `.env` is gitignored and never committed (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md`).
- Commit `.env.example`: every key the tool reads, placeholder or empty values, a comment per key.
- Keys `UPPER_SNAKE` with the tool prefix (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/NAMING.md`).
- One `KEY=value` per line: no spaces around `=`, no `export`, quote values containing spaces.
- Optional: the tool runs without it; env vars keep their place in config precedence (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/JSON.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.json
---
## JSON
> Load when: writing, generating or validating a JSON file or JSON output.

- UTF-8 without BOM, 2-space indent, trailing newline.
- Strict JSON: no comments, no trailing commas; JSONC or JSON5 only where the reading tool documents it.
- Generated files: stable key order and formatting, so regeneration diffs only real changes.
- Schema exists → `$schema` key first; write schemas in JSON Schema draft 2020-12.
- Validate in CI: `jq empty <file>` at minimum, plus the schema when one exists (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`).
- Machine-written config: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`. CLI output: `--json` per `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CLI.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/FRONTMATTER.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.markdown.frontmatter
---
## Markdown frontmatter
> Load when: adding YAML frontmatter to a Markdown file.

- Only when a tool reads it: skills (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SKILL-MD.md`), Cursor `.mdc`, Copilot `.instructions.md`, Kiro steering, static site generators.
- Fenced by `---` starting on line 1; nothing before it.
- Flat keys with string values unless the tool's schema says otherwise; YAML rules: `CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/YAML.md`.
- Only keys the tool documents; no custom metadata the tool ignores.
- Never secrets, tokens or personal data.
- Ordinary rule files use their rule header (`# Title`, then `> Load when:`) instead of tool frontmatter; their front matter holds only rule keys such as `id` (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/RULE-FILES.md`).

### Minimal SKILL.md

`release-notes/SKILL.md`: `---` on line 1, only the documented `name` and `description` keys, then the body.

```markdown
---
name: release-notes
description: Drafts release notes from merged pull requests. Use when preparing a release, tagging a version, or summarizing changes since the last tag.
---
Collect merged pull requests since the last tag and group them by type.
```

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/GITHUB-EXTRAS.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.markdown.github-extras
---
## GitHub Markdown extras
> Load when: using alerts, collapsible sections, task lists, diagrams, footnotes, badges or images in Markdown rendered on GitHub.

- Alerts (`> [!NOTE]`, `> [!TIP]`, `> [!IMPORTANT]`, `> [!WARNING]`, `> [!CAUTION]`): sparingly, one or two per page, never stacked.
- `<details><summary>…</summary>` for long optional content (logs, full option lists); never hide install or required steps.
- Task lists (`- [ ]`, `- [x]`) for checklists in issues, PRs and plans.
- Diagrams: a fenced `mermaid` block instead of an image, so it diffs and stays editable.
- Footnotes (`[^1]`) for sources and asides that would break a line.
- No `:emoji:` shortcodes in specs, rules or docs.
- Badges: shields.io in the palette (`CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`); placement per `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`.
- Images: alt text always; `<img src="…" alt="…" width="…">` when size matters.
- Screenshots may use `github.com/user-attachments` URLs from an issue or PR upload instead of committed binaries.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/STYLE.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.markdown.style
---
## Markdown style
> Load when: writing or editing any Markdown file.

- Target GitHub-Flavored Markdown.
- ATX headings (`#`); one `#` per file; never skip a level.
- Bullets with `-`; numbered lists only when order matters.
- Fenced code blocks with a language tag (`sh`, `go`, `toml`, `text`).
- One sentence or rule per line; never hard-wrap mid-sentence (clean diffs).
- No trailing spaces, no `\` or two-space line breaks; a blank line separates blocks.
- Relative links inside a repo; name files and paths in backticks.
- Language and voice: `CONVENTIONS/REPO/WRITING.md`.
- markdownlint defaults apply, minus line length (MD013) and any rule these lines override.
- Frontmatter, tables, GitHub extras: `CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/FRONTMATTER.md`, `CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/TABLES.md`, `CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/GITHUB-EXTRAS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/MARKDOWN/TABLES.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.markdown.tables
---
## Markdown tables
> Load when: adding a table to a Markdown file.

- Table only for 3+ parallel attributes per row; otherwise a list.
- Header row plus `|---|` separator; first column is the key.
- Escape a literal pipe in a cell as `\|`.
- Short cells: a value or phrase, no paragraphs or lists; link out for detail.
- No merged or empty structural cells; one fact per cell.
- Wide tables are fine: GitHub scrolls them horizontally; never split one table into several to fit.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/TOML.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.toml
---
## TOML
> Load when: writing or parsing a TOML file.

- TOML 1.0; default format for human-edited config, every key commented (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`).
- Keys `snake_case` (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/NAMING.md`); bare keys, quoted only when required.
- `[table]` sections over inline tables; inline tables only for short one-line values.
- Arrays of records as `[[array]]`, not nested inline arrays.
- Dates and times as TOML datetimes (RFC 3339), never strings.
- Durations and sizes carry units: a string (`"30s"`, `"10MiB"`) or a key suffix (`timeout_secs`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/FORMATS/YAML.md -->
---
id: conventions.formats.yaml
---
## YAML
> Load when: writing a GitHub workflow, issue form, compose file, frontmatter, or any YAML a tool requires.

- Only where a tool demands it (Actions workflows, issue forms, compose, frontmatter); never for authored config (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`).
- 2-space indent, no tabs; `.yml` unless the tool requires `.yaml`.
- Quote strings that parse as other types: versions (`'3.10'`, else `3.1`), `'on'`/`'off'`/`'yes'`/`'no'` values, leading zeros, `'*'`.
- Workflows: share steps via reusable workflows or composite actions (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`), not anchors and aliases.
- Block style over flow style (`[a, b]`), except short lists.
- CI: `actionlint` for workflows, `yamllint` for other YAML.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.actions.ci
---
## CI
> Load when: setting up or changing CI checks or required status checks, or fixing a red CI run.

- `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs on every push and PR, without a `paths:` filter.
- It runs format + lint, build, tests, package build, docs-in-sync; cheap steps first, fail fast, no `continue-on-error` on required steps.
- Lint per stack: `shellcheck` for shell, `go vet` + `gofmt -l` for Go, the ecosystem's standard linter elsewhere.
- Package build: `PKGBUILD` in an Arch container, `nix build` when a flake ships (`CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`, `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md`).
- Docs-in-sync: regenerate generated files, `--help` output and completions, then `git diff --exit-code`.
- Tests run on throwaway state (temp `HOME`, temp dirs), never on real user config.
- Required checks (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`) match job names: keep them stable; renaming a job blocks merges until the ruleset is updated.
- On failure, upload logs and test output: `actions/upload-artifact` with `if: failure()` and a short `retention-days`.
- CI never pushes to `main`; bots open PRs and are listed in one place (README "Automation" section). Bot PRs need a GitHub App token: `GITHUB_TOKEN` PRs start no checks.
- Schedule keepalive: after ~45 quiet days the scheduled job runs `gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows/<file>/enable` (`actions: write`); no commit, no ruleset bypass. Disabled anyway → `gh workflow enable <file>`.
- No ruleset bypass actors for bots (repo rulesets also reject the GitHub Actions app as one).
- Red CI: read `gh run view <id> --log-failed`, reproduce with the local script, fix, push; never rerun until green.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.actions.workflows
---
## Workflows
> Load when: writing or editing a GitHub Actions workflow, reusable workflow or composite action.

- One purpose per file in `.github/workflows/`: `check.yml` (CI), `release.yml` (releases), `pages.yml` (site).
- Triggers: `push` + `pull_request` for checks; add `workflow_dispatch` to anything worth rerunning by hand.
- `schedule` only for data from outside the repo; public repos disable it after 60 days without activity, so add a keepalive (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`).
- Cross-repo triggers: `repository_dispatch` with a named `types:` entry.
- Top-level `permissions: contents: read`; elevate per job only (`contents: write`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`).
- `concurrency:` group per workflow + ref; `cancel-in-progress: true` for checks, `false` for deploys and releases.
- Pin actions to a major tag (`actions/*`) or a full commit SHA with a `# vX` comment (third-party); Dependabot keeps them current (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md`).
- Logic lives in repo scripts that run locally (Docker/Podman when the host differs); the workflow only checks out, sets up and calls them.
- Pass `${{ }}` values into `run:` through `env:`, never inline (script injection).
- Secrets only via `secrets.*` or OIDC (`id-token: write`); never echo them or put them on a command line; mask derived values with `::add-mask::`.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` over PATs. Events it causes start no workflows (except `workflow_dispatch`/`repository_dispatch`) and it cannot reach other repos; for those cases only, use a GitHub App token (`actions/create-github-app-token`) or a fine-grained PAT scoped to the target repo.
- Same steps in 2+ repos → reusable workflow (`on: workflow_call`) or composite action in one org repo, called pinned.
- Results people read go to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` as Markdown, not only to logs.
- Minutes: public repos run free on standard runners, private repos on GitHub Free get 2,000 min/month; keep matrices to supported targets, cache dependencies (`actions/cache` or a setup action's `cache:`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.code-security
---
## Code security
> Load when: creating a repo, adding dependencies, or handling Dependabot, secret-scanning or code-scanning alerts.

- Dependabot alerts and security updates on for every repo.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: version updates for `github-actions` plus each package ecosystem, `interval: weekly`, `groups:` to batch minor/patch.
- Dependabot PRs follow the normal PR flow; merge when CI is green, never skip checks.
- Secret scanning + push protection on (`gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning --enable-secret-scanning-push-protection`; free for public repos).
- Leaked secret: rotate it first, then remove it; history rewriting needs owner approval.
- CodeQL default setup for supported languages (free for public repos); fix or dismiss alerts with a reason.
- Private vulnerability reporting on for public repos; policy file: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SECURITY-MD.md`.
- Never commit secrets, tokens or `.env` files; workflows read them per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODING-AGENTS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.coding-agents
---
## Coding agents on GitHub
> Load when: assigning issues to a coding agent, @-mentioning an agent on GitHub, or running an agent from a workflow.

- Agents: Copilot coding agent (assign an issue; needs a paid Copilot plan), Claude Code / Codex GitHub apps or actions (@-mention or workflow).
- Agent PRs follow the same rules: titles per `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md`, flow per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PULL-REQUESTS.md`.
- Branch names per `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md` where the tool allows (e.g. a branch-prefix input); fixed tool prefixes are accepted.
- Agent PRs stay draft until checks are green; a human or the orchestrating agent reviews and merges, never the agent itself unasked.
- Instructions come from the repo `AGENTS.md`; `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` are generated from it (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/AGENTS-MD.md`).
- Issue for an agent: one task, acceptance criteria, files or commands to run; same as for a human.
- Least-privilege tokens: repo-scoped, contents + pull requests + issues only; workflow `permissions:` set explicitly.
- Never put secrets in prompts, issues or comments; agents read them from Actions secrets only.
- Untrusted input (issues or comments from strangers) never triggers an agent with write access.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/ENVIRONMENTS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.deployments.environments
---
## Deployment environments
> Load when: deploying anything from Actions, or adding deployment secrets.

- Every deploy job declares `environment:` with `name` (`github-pages`, `production`) and `url` from the deploy step's output.
- Deployment branches: `main` only (tags `v*` for release deploys).
- Secrets used only by one deploy are environment secrets, not repo secrets.
- Required reviewers or wait timers only when a second human can approve; solo repos rely on the branch policy.
- GitHub Free: environment secrets and branch policies work in public repos only; private repos use repo secrets and deploy only from `main`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/GITHUB-PAGES.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.deployments.github-pages
---
## GitHub Pages
> Load when: publishing a site, docs or web UI on GitHub Pages.

- Source "GitHub Actions" (`gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -f build_type=workflow`); never a `gh-pages` branch.
- Build job → `actions/upload-pages-artifact`; deploy job → `actions/deploy-pages` with `pages: write`, `id-token: write`, environment `github-pages` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/ENVIRONMENTS.md`).
- Never commit build output; the output dir (`public/`) is gitignored.
- Build script lives in the repo and gives the same result locally; the workflow only calls it.
- Output: one self-contained `index.html` (CSS, JS, data inlined) that works offline and over `file://`.
- Next to it: the same data as JSON; docs sites also ship `llms.txt` (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LLMS-TXT.md`).
- Deploy only from `main`; triggers: push on source paths, `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch` for refreshes from other repos.
- Nightly `schedule` only when data comes from outside the repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`).
- Repo homepage = the Pages URL unless a real site exists (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`).
- Custom domain only when one is owned: set it in Pages settings (`gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -f cname=<domain>`); Actions deploys ignore a `CNAME` file.
- Look and layout: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/THEME.md` and `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/LAYOUT.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/WEBUI-STYLE.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.deployments.webui-style
---
## Web UI style
> Load when: building or restyling a project web page, Pages site or web UI.
> Superseded by: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/THEME.md`, `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/LAYOUT.md`, `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/COMPONENTS.md`, `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/ACCESSIBILITY.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DISCUSSIONS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.discussions
---
## Discussions
> Load when: enabling GitHub Discussions, choosing categories, or moving threads between issues and discussions.

- Enable only when the project has users beyond its maintainers (`gh repo edit --enable-discussions`); otherwise issues suffice.
- Categories: Announcements (maintainers post), Ideas, Q&A (answerable), Show and tell; delete unused defaults. Categories are web-UI only (no REST/GraphQL mutation).
- Issues are actionable work; questions, ideas and open-ended talk are discussions.
- Convert a non-actionable issue to a discussion; open an issue from a discussion once work is agreed, linking both ways.
- Accepted idea → proposal PR on an experimental branch (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md`); link the discussion in the PR.
- Q&A: mark the answer; turn repeated questions into docs.
- Release and breaking-change notes go to Announcements.
- CLI: `gh discussion list/view/create/comment` (preview); otherwise `gh api graphql`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ISSUES.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.issues
---
## Issues
> Load when: creating, triaging or closing issues, or adding issue templates.

- Issue forms: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/<name>.yml` (bug, feature) with `labels:` preset; org default in the org `.github` repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`: `blank_issues_enabled: false`; `contact_links` to Discussions, docs or support.
- Title: imperative, specific, no type prefix (`Fix crash on empty config`, `Add --json to list`); type goes in the label.
- Label on creation (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`); set the issue type when the org defines types (`--type Bug`).
- Split work into sub-issues (`gh issue create --parent <n>`, `gh issue edit <n> --add-sub-issue <m>`); short checklists stay `- [ ]` task lists.
- Dependencies: `--blocked-by <n>` / `--blocking <n>`, not prose.
- Close via the PR: `Closes #<n>` in the PR body; keywords only fire when the PR targets the default branch.
- Closing without a PR: comment why, close as not planned or duplicate (`gh issue close <n> -r "not planned" -c "<why>"`).
- Roadmap: one issue with sub-issues, pinned (`gh issue pin <n>`); max 3 pinned.
- Agents: `gh issue list/view/create/edit/comment` with `--json`; never close an issue you did not resolve.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.organizations
---
## Organizations
> Load when: creating or maintaining a GitHub organization, its profile, teams, or org-wide defaults.

- Org profile: public `.github` repo with `profile/README.md` (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`).
- Org `.github` repo holds default community health files, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; repos override only when they differ.
- Access through teams with least privilege, never per-person grants on each repo.
- Pin up to 6 flagship repos on the org profile.
- Every repo: consistent name (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/NAMING.md`), description, homepage, topics (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`).
- Same labels and settings everywhere (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`, `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`).
- Cross-repo planning: org-level Projects (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PROJECTS.md`).
- Org settings, membership and repo visibility: owner approval first.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PROJECTS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.projects
---
## Projects
> Load when: planning work across issues, creating or editing a GitHub Project board.

- Projects (v2) only; one per org or per initiative, not one per repo.
- Items are issues and PRs; draft items only for quick capture, converted to issues before work starts.
- Fields: Status (Todo, In progress, Done), Priority (P0–P2), Size (S/M/L), Iteration when working in cycles.
- Views: Board grouped by Status, Table for triage, Roadmap by Iteration or dates.
- Built-in workflows: auto-add matching repo issues/PRs, item added → Todo, item closed and PR merged → Done.
- Status follows issues and PRs (open, linked PR, closed), not hand-moved cards.
- Link the project to its repos (`gh project link`).
- CLI: `gh project view/item-list/item-add/item-edit/field-list --owner <org>`; needs the `project` scope (`gh auth refresh -s project`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PULL-REQUESTS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.pull-requests
---
## Pull requests
> Load when: committing, pushing, or opening/reviewing/merging a PR.

- Self-review before PR: correctness, security/escaping, docs + shell completions in sync.
- Work in progress → draft PR (`gh pr create --draft`); `gh pr ready` only when done and self-reviewed.
- Body follows `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (what, why, checks run); org default: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`.
- Link issues with `Closes #<n>` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ISSUES.md`); label on creation (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`).
- Review: concrete fixes as suggested changes (a `suggestion` code block); the author batch-applies them as one commit.
- Wait for green CI → `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch` or `--rebase --delete-branch` (never `--squash`) → `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only` → verify main CI + live result → one short report.
- Never `--admin`, never merge locally into `main`; every change reaches `main` through a PR.
- PRs from non-maintainers: only a maintainer reviews and merges them; agents never approve or merge them, even when CI is green.
- Branch behind or conflicting → `git merge origin/main` into it (or `gh pr update-branch`) and push; still conflicting → ask before rebasing locally and force-pushing the branch.
- Never merge red, force-push, or bypass branch protection; repo settings: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`.
- What CI runs and requires: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`; workflow files: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`.
- Commit and PR titles: `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/AUTOMATION.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.releases.automation
---
## Release automation
> Load when: writing or running a release workflow or script, attaching release assets, or bumping downstream packages.

- Default: a human pushes the tag (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md`); `.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest.
- Trigger `on: push: tags: ['v*']`, plus `workflow_dispatch` with a tag input for reruns.
- Manual retries build from the selected tag but use the release coordinator script from the workflow commit on `main`, so a workflow fix can safely verify an immutable release without changing its tagged source tree.
- A tag pushed by a workflow with `GITHUB_TOKEN` triggers nothing; dispatch the release instead (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`).
- `contents: write` on the release job only.
- Build every asset on CI from the tag; never upload local builds.
- Attach assets + `SHA256SUMS` (`sha256sum <assets> > SHA256SUMS`), plus a signature (`SHA256SUMS.sig`) when the project signs.
- Publish: `gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --notes-from-tag <assets>`; no curated notes → `--generate-notes`; `-rc.N` → add `--prerelease`.
- `.github/release.yml` groups generated notes by label (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`): `changelog.categories` for `feat`, `bug`, `docs`, `chore`, last one `"*"`.
- Release logic is a repo script that runs locally with `--dry-run`: builds, checksums, prints the `gh` commands without publishing.
- Downstream bumps after publish: package metadata and `flake.nix` via PR, or `repository_dispatch` to the packaging repo.
- Verify: `gh release view "$TAG"` lists every asset, checksums match, downstream PRs green.
- Release-please style automation only when the project uses Conventional Commits strictly (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.releases.channels
---
## Release channels
> Load when: deciding where a build is published: stable, pre-release, experimental or nightly.

| Channel | Built from | Tag | GitHub release |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stable | `main` | `vX.Y.Z` | Normal, marked Latest |
| Pre-release | `main` | `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | `--prerelease` |
| Experimental | any other branch | none | none |
| Nightly (optional) | `main`, scheduled | `nightly`, rolling | `--prerelease --latest=false` |

- Latest = newest stable; never mark a pre-release or nightly as latest.
- Experimental: `-ex` in package name or version, installs next to stable; ships as workflow artifacts or a package channel (Arch: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`).
- Nightly is the only tag and release that is re-created: `gh release delete nightly --cleanup-tag -y`, then `gh release create nightly --target main --prerelease --latest=false`.
- Nightly only when people test unreleased builds; skip the run when `main` has not changed.
- Install docs point at stable; other channels are opt-in.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.releases.tags
---
## Tags
> Load when: creating, pushing, protecting or fixing a release tag.

- Signed and annotated only: `git tag -s vX.Y.Z -F <notes-file>`; never lightweight. The `release-tags` ruleset must require signatures.
- Format `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`); pre-releases `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`.
- Tag `main` only, on a commit whose CI is green.
- `-ex` builds are never tagged `v*` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`).
- Tag message: title `vX.Y.Z`, then that version's changelog section.
- Push one tag explicitly: `git push origin vX.Y.Z`; never `git push --tags`.
- Published tags are immutable: never move, delete or re-push one; fix a bad release with a new patch tag.
- Only exception: the rolling `nightly` tag (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`).
- Protect with a tag ruleset (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets`): `target: tag`, `conditions.ref_name.include: ["refs/tags/v*"]`, rules `update` + `deletion`; `nightly` stays outside it.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.releases.versioning
---
## Releases & versioning
> Load when: bumping a version, preparing a release, or planning a major version.

- SemVer `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Tags: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md`; publishing: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/AUTOMATION.md`; channels: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`.
- The version lives in package metadata and tags; never in the README title or repo name.
- One bump moves every copy at once: source constant, PKGBUILD `pkgver`, `flake.nix` `version`, changelog if the project keeps one.
- Breaking change to a command, flag, config key or file format → major bump, plus a new `docs/ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` when the project keeps one.
- Profile eras are independent of project versions.
- Before tagging: versions agree; `--help`, completions and README match the code; tests pass on throwaway state; the package builds in CI; the architecture contract is current.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.repo.labels
---
## Labels
> Load when: creating, editing or applying issue/PR labels, or setting up a new repo.

- Keep the set small; plain names, no `type:` prefixes, so `--force` recolors the matching GitHub defaults (`bug`, `good first issue`, `help wanted`).
- Other defaults stay (never delete): use the profile's secondary color, description `Deprecated: use <label>` (`documentation` → `docs`, `enhancement` → `feat`).

| Label | Color | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `bug` `feat` `docs` `chore` | `the project's configured accent` | Type, one per issue/PR |
| `area/<x>` | `1b1b1b` | Per-project subsystem, defined in the project |
| `breaking` | `the project's configured danger color` | Major bump; its own section in release notes |
| `experimental` | `the project's configured danger color` | Proposal on an experimental branch |
| `legacy` | `the project's configured secondary color` | Superseded material |
| `blocked` | `the project's configured danger text color` | Waiting on something external |
| `good first issue` | `the project's configured highlight color` | Easy entry; the one highlight color |
| `help wanted` | `the project's configured accent text color` | Maintainer wants outside help |

- Colors come from `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`, hex without `#`; replace unsuitable platform defaults.
- Labels as code: a script or `labels.tsv` in the repo, applied with `gh label create <name> -c <hex> -d <desc> --force`.
- Same set across an org: `gh label clone <source-repo> --force`.
- Never delete or rename a label others use; mark it deprecated in its description first.
- Label on creation (`gh issue create -l`, `gh pr create -l`), not afterwards.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.repo.metadata
---
## Repo metadata
> Load when: creating a repo, first push, release, or editing README/manifest/license.

- `gh repo view` first; fill gaps via `gh repo edit`: description, homepage, topics, badges (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`).
- Homepage priority: real site → GitHub Pages → repo URL. Never invent.
- Keep manifest fields (package.json, go.mod, PKGBUILD, flake.nix…) in sync with repo metadata.
- License: MIT; awesome lists CC0 (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/AWESOME-LIST.md`).
- Fork of someone else's project: say "independent, not affiliated" in the README and the description; add a trademark note when the upstream name is a mark.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.repo.settings
---
## Repo settings
> Load when: creating a repo, changing its GitHub settings, merge options, rulesets or feature toggles.

- Apply settings as code: `gh repo edit` flags and `gh api` calls in a script, not web-UI clicks. Metadata: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`.
- Default branch `main` (`--default-branch main`); branch model: `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md`.
- Merge: merge commit or rebase, never squash (`--enable-merge-commit --enable-rebase-merge --enable-squash-merge=false`): branch commits land on `main` as written and trailers (`Co-Authored-By:`) survive.
- `--delete-branch-on-merge`, `--enable-auto-merge`, `--allow-update-branch`.
- Ruleset on the default branch via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets` (`gh ruleset` only lists, views, checks):
  - `pull_request` with 0 required approvals and `allowed_merge_methods: ["merge", "rebase"]`: PR required, every maintainer reviews and self-merges; no `required_linear_history` (it blocks merge commits).
  - `required_status_checks`: only checks that run on every PR; a path-filtered or not-yet-existing check blocks merges forever.
  - Public repo with outside contributors: also require `review-gate`, a commit status set from trusted triggers (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run`, schedule) that passes maintainer PRs and other PRs only after a maintainer approves the head commit; `.github/CODEOWNERS` requests the review. Reference: `META/tools/review-gate.sh`.
- Fork PR workflows: approval for all outside contributors (`actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval`, `all_external_contributors`).
  - `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`, `required_linear_history`.
- Rulesets are free on public repos; private repos on GitHub Free get none, so the PR flow is self-enforced there.
- Features: issues on; discussions only for a community (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DISCUSSIONS.md`); projects per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PROJECTS.md`; wiki off (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/WIKI.md`).
- Security toggles: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md`.
- Visibility change, transfer, archive or rename: owner approval first; never pass `--accept-visibility-change-consequences` on your own.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/WIKI.md -->
---
id: conventions.github.wiki
---
## Wiki
> Load when: enabling a GitHub wiki or deciding where project docs live.

- Docs live in the repo (versioned, reviewed via PR) and on Pages; the repo is the source of truth.
- Wiki off by default (`gh repo edit --enable-wiki=false`).
- Wiki only if users expect one: generate or sync it from repo docs in CI; never edit it by hand.
- The wiki never holds rules, specs or anything not also in the repo.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CLI.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.cli
---
## CLI
> Load when: building or changing a command-line tool.

- One binary, one entry point, rich subcommands + flags + config file (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`).
- Colored per-command help; aligned tables. Colors: `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`.
- Message prefixes: `::` info, `==>` step, `✓` ok, `!!` warn, `✗` error. Messages to stderr, data to stdout.
- `--no-color` and `NO_COLOR`; plain output when stdout is not a TTY.
- `--json` for data output.
- Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` error, `2` usage error.
- `completion <shell>` + installed zsh/bash/fish completion files, generated from the command registry.
- Destructive commands confirm (or take `--yes`) and support `--dry-run`.
- Root: `the platform-supported privilege mechanism` for the one step that needs it; never use an unsafe privilege shortcut.
- Has a CLI → also needs a TUI: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/TUI.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.config
---
## Configuration
> Load when: adding a config file, options, env vars, or storage paths to a tool.

- Human-edited: TOML, every option commented with its default. Machine-written: strict JSON (reject unknown keys).
- Avoid YAML for authored config (whitespace and type footguns); use it only where a tool demands it.
- Precedence, later wins: built-in defaults < config file < `*.local.*` override (gitignored) < env `TOOL_*` < flags.
- XDG paths: config `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/<tool>/`, data `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/<tool>/`, cache and state likewise. Shipped defaults stay separate from the user layer.
- Runs with zero config; an option exists only where two real users need different behavior.
- Validate on load; invalid → a clear error naming file and key, nothing applied. Never guess or coerce.
- Secrets never in config: reference an env var, file path or keyring entry by name.
- Local persistence: SQLite (WAL) when there is real data, else a plain file.
- Colors configurable when the project has config (`CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/TUI.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.tui
---
## TUI
> Load when: building a TUI, or any project that has a CLI.

- Go: bubbletea + lipgloss + bubbles + glamour.
- Thin front-end over the same commands and functions as the CLI; no logic lives only in the TUI.
- Fully keyboard-driven; mouse is a bonus.
- `:` command palette, help overlay (`?` / F1), keybinds shown in a footer.
- Tabs per item type; add / edit / toggle / remove in place, destructive actions confirmed.
- Markdown rendered with glamour.
- Colors: `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`.

---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.accessibility
---
## Web UI accessibility
> Load when: making a web UI usable with keyboard, assistive technology or accessibility preferences.

- Meet WCAG AA contrast in every theme, show keyboard focus and make targets at least 26px tall.
- Add a skip link; use `role="tab"` and `tabpanel` for tabs and `aria-current` on the active index item.
- Under `prefers-contrast: more`, raise muted text and line contrast; keep selection visible in `forced-colors` mode.
- Keep effects subtle (hover underline or glow, blinking cursor, carousel glide, faint terminal scanlines) and disable them under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- Do not track users or use analytics or cookies; load external JavaScript only when unavoidable, from an exact-version CDN URL with `integrity`.
- Give every interactive element a visible label or an `aria-label`; add a `title` to icon-only buttons.
- Check each theme with `prefers-contrast: more`, `forced-colors: active` and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/ARCHITECTURE.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.architecture
---
## Web UI architecture
> Load when: building a web UI, docs site or Pages site from scratch, or restructuring its build or page code.

Reference implementation: `META/tools/site.sh`. Visual rules: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/THEME.md` and `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/LAYOUT.md`. Components and accessibility: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/COMPONENTS.md` and `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/ACCESSIBILITY.md`. Starter: `TEMPLATES/webui.html`.

- One self-contained `index.html`: markup, CSS and JS inline. No framework, no bundler, no runtime build step.
- A build script collects every source into one data object and writes it into the page as `<script type="application/json" id="data">`, with `<` escaped as `<`.
- Build-time values reach the page only through that data block. Never interpolate them into HTML or JS (quote the heredocs).
- The page works offline and over `file://`. Content never depends on a runtime request.
- Live data (stars, latest release) is optional: show the build-time value, fetch once, keep the value on any failure. No retries, no spinners.
- A small inline `<head>` script sets the theme before first paint.
- State is a few top-level variables (view, filter, open item). One `render()` rebuilds the view from state and data. Handlers change state, then call `render()` or set the hash.
- Escape every data string before it enters HTML (`esc()`). Render Markdown with a small local renderer.
- No tracking, analytics or cookies; external JS only when unavoidable, from a CDN URL pinned to an exact version with `integrity`.
- One sprite of inline SVG icons, defined once and used with `<use>`.
- Output goes to a gitignored directory (`public/`) and CI deploys it (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/GITHUB-PAGES.md`). Never commit it.
- Verify: build, open over `file://` and over HTTP, try each deep link and each key, check 360px width and every theme.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/COMPONENTS.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.components
---
## Web UI components
> Load when: building a carousel, filter, menu, modal, popup, install panel or icon set for a web UI.

- Show the "Compatible with" carousel only when it has registry entries; include an icon or monogram, name and muted label.
- Drive one slow continuous carousel glide with `requestAnimationFrame`; move right on 1% of page loads, pause while hidden and ease back after interaction.
- Use seamless `aria-hidden` clones with `tabindex="-1"` and edge-fade masks; hover, focus or touch eases the glide to a stop for wheel, trackpad, drag or swipe scrolling with wraparound.
- Under reduced motion, show a static scrollable carousel without clones.
- Open a compatibility popup by clicking an item or rule chip, pressing `Enter`, or loading `#compat/<id>`; show icon or monogram, name, kind, description, compatible version, versioning note, added and updated dates, covering rules linked by `#<path>`, external links in a new tab and a muted registry disclaimer.
- Show segmented `All · Third-party · the project` origin tabs only where rules have origin tags; filter that tab's rules, combine with text filtering, update counts and status, badge each row and show third-party registry chips.
- Use a top-right `[MENU]` disclosure with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; arrows, `Home` and `End` move through actions and links; close it on outside click, `Esc`, Tab out or item activation.
- Reuse one native `<dialog>` with a vignette `::backdrop` and `showModal()`; close on `Esc`, backdrop click or close button, return focus to its opener, and scroll inside at 320px.
- Highlight filter hits with accent-tinted `<mark>`, flag matching tabs and announce the result count in an `aria-live` status.
- Put the tagline, stats and one wrapping copyable command block in the install modal; open it from `[MENU]` or `#install`; show the copy icon as a check for about 1s.
- Define 14–16px inline SVG icons once in a sprite with `currentColor`; inline registry icons at build time as filled paths; use no icon fonts, `<img>` icons, icon CDNs or brand colors.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/KEYBOARD.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.keyboard
---
## Web UI keyboard
> Load when: adding keyboard shortcuts or keyboard navigation to a web UI.

- One `keydown` listener on `window` owns the single-key shortcuts. It ignores events with Ctrl, Meta or Alt.
- Gate order: modal open, the dialog owns the keys. Menu open, only `Esc`. Focus in a widget with its own keys (tab list, carousel), the widget. Focus in a text field, only `Esc`.
- Default map: `/` focus the filter, `1`–`9` and `0` switch views, `t` theme, `e` expand all, `?` key help, `Esc` close the top layer, then clear the filter.
- Widgets follow the WAI-ARIA patterns (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/>): tabs and menus move with arrows, `Home` and `End`.
- Every shortcut has a visible control. Key help lists the map from the same table that the handler reads.
- Never bind keys that the browser or a screen reader reserves: Ctrl/Cmd combinations, Tab, Space outside buttons.
- Focus is always visible. After a view switch, focus stays on the control that caused it.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/LAYOUT.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.layout
---
## Web UI layout
> Load when: laying out a web page or arranging its header, navigation and content.

- Center a one-line `h1` at up to 3.3rem, scale it to fit 320px without wrapping, omit the hero and tagline, add a `❯` prompt and a 3–4px accent top rule; put the byline in the footer.
- Order the navbar as title, non-empty "Compatible with" carousel, full-width tabs, then filter.
- Keep folder tabs and filter in a sticky toolbar.
- Use collapsible nested groups with counts and a category index; show the index as a sidebar when wide and a disclosure when narrow.
- At 360px, prevent horizontal page scroll; contain wide tables and code in their own scrolling boxes.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/OVERLAYS.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.overlays
---
## Web UI overlays
> Load when: adding a modal, popup, menu, copy button or share action to a web UI.

- One native `<dialog>` per page, reused through one `openModal({title, html, opener, onClose})`. Open it with `showModal()`.
- The dialog closes on `Esc`, on a backdrop click and on its close button. Focus returns to the opener.
- Popup content comes from the build-time data object. No fetch to open a popup.
- Menu: a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) and a list. Arrows, `Home` and `End` move. It closes on an outside click, `Esc` and Tab out.
- The modal stacks over the menu. `Esc` closes the top layer first.
- Every overlay has a transient deep link (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/ROUTING.md`).
- Copy buttons copy the literal value, swap the icon to a check for about 1 s, and stay unchanged on failure.
- Share: the page URL with the current hash, a copy button and plain links. No third-party share scripts.
- The dialog scrolls inside itself at 360px width. The page behind it does not scroll.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/ROUTING.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.routing
---
## Web UI routing
> Load when: adding views, deep links or URL handling to a web UI.

- The URL hash is the router: `#<view>`, `#<item-path>`, `#<group>/`. `hashchange` calls `route()`, `route()` sets state, then calls `render()`.
- Every view, group and item has a deep link. Loading it restores the view, opens the item and scrolls it below the sticky bar (`scroll-margin-top`).
- Unknown hash: show the first view. No error page.
- Old hashes keep working: `route()` maps retired ids to their new target.
- Overlay routes are transient (`#install`, `#about`, `#<kind>/<id>`): set them with `history.replaceState`, render the view under the overlay, restore the previous hash on close.
- A content link inside an overlay closes the overlay and moves focus to the target, not to the opener.
- Filter text and toggles stay out of the hash. A deep link clears the filter.
- The hash carries routes only. A skip link moves focus without changing the hash.
- Query parameters only for view options that are not saved (`?theme=`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/WEBUI/THEME.md -->
---
id: conventions.interfaces.webui.theme
---
## Web UI theme
> Load when: choosing colors, themes, typography or visual effects for a web UI.

- Use colors only from `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md` as CSS custom properties on `:root`, overridden per `[data-theme]`.
- Follow the project's published design reference when one exists.
- Provide `dark` (default) and `light` themes; `mono` (greys and silver, no accent hue) and `terminal` (near-black, accent-text headings and links) are optional.
- Set `data-theme` on `<html>` before first paint; expose theme choice in `[MENU]` and on `t`; save it in `localStorage` inside `try`/`catch`; on first visit follow `prefers-color-scheme`, else use dark.
- Use `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`; never fetch webfonts.
- Use a flat mono/material look: 1px lines, 0–4px radius, no gradients except modal vignette and carousel edge-fade masks, no glassmorphism or heavy shadows.
- Show depth through the surface and line ramps in `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`; frame groups as panels and give an opened item a sunken reading well with an accent edge.
- Set body text to 14px, copy to 13–13.5px at line-height 1.6–1.7, minimum text to 11.5px and reading width to 92ch.

---
id: conventions.packaging.arch
---
## Arch packaging
> Load when: packaging, releasing, or adding install instructions.

- Ship a `PKGBUILD` (repo root or a packaging subdirectory) that installs: binary, shell completions, license, docs.
- `the project's package registry` builds every PKGBUILD in the project; stable and experimental channels follow the registry's policy.
- Override the package channel with the registry's documented setting.
- VCS packages: `pkgver()` yielding `r<count>.<hash>`.
- Packages, databases and install scripts are signed; clients use `SigLevel = Required`.
- Version moves with the release (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- Nix counterpart: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md`. Installers: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/INSTALL.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/INSTALL.md -->
---
id: conventions.packaging.install
---
## Install & uninstall
> Load when: writing an installer, a setup script, install instructions, or uninstall steps.

- Package first (`the project's package registry`, Nix); a script installer only for what a package cannot do (user config, harness links).
- Reversible: ship and document uninstall; it restores what install changed.
- Own one prefix (`~/.local/share/<tool>`, or one folder in portable mode); outside it, touch at most one documented hook line.
- By default, preserve global instruction files and update only a marked block or import line; uninstall removes only that block. A `--replace` option may back up and replace a file only when the user explicitly opts in.
- Idempotent: re-running converges and never duplicates.
- `status` and `--dry-run` show what would change before anything does.
- Verifiable sources: a tag or a signed script, never a branch tip piped into a shell.
- Root: `the platform-supported privilege mechanism` for the one step that needs it, never for the whole script.
- Scripts follow `CONVENTIONS/CODE/SHELL.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md -->
---
id: conventions.packaging.nix
---
## Nix packaging
> Load when: packaging, releasing, or setting up a dev environment.

- Ship `flake.nix` with: package, app, devShell.
- `version` in the flake moves with the release (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- Arch counterpart: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`.

---
id: conventions.profiles.overlays
---
## Profile overlays
> Load when: selecting a profile or applying team, project or user-specific rule overrides.

- Precedence is core defaults < organization profile < team overlay < project overlay < user overlay; a later string value replaces the earlier value.
- Put overlays in TOML files with `[overrides]`, `disable = ["<stable-rule-id>"]`, and an optional `[overrides.set]` table of `profile.<variable> = "<value>"` entries.
- Disable rules by stable `id`, never by path; a disabled rule is omitted from generated indexes and bundles.
- Render layers in order with `META/tools/build.sh --profile <name> --team <file> --project <file> --user <file>`; omit unused layers.
- Keep personal settings in the user overlay, team defaults in the team overlay, and repository-specific choices in the project overlay.
- Overlay values are strings; define new variables in the profile template before referencing them in a rule.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/REPO/DOCS.md -->
---
id: conventions.repo.docs
---
## Docs structure
> Load when: writing or restructuring a README, guide or docs page, or filling the body of one of its sections.

Section order: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`. Voice: `CONVENTIONS/REPO/WRITING.md`. Voice profile and examples: `AGENTS/PROMPT/DOCS-VOICE.md`. Skeleton: `TEMPLATES/project-README.md`.

- Open: `# Name`, one bold sentence that says what it is and for whom, one plain sentence that says what the reader gets. Facts only: count, scope, platform.
- More than one guide → a "Start here" table first: guide, what it covers, when to read it. Mark the one to read first.
- Topic map: two-column table `Topic | What you learn`, one row per topic, ≤ 8 rows.
- What's inside: annotated tree in a `text` block; one entry per line, comments aligned in one column, ≤ 2 levels unless the third level teaches something.
- Install: `Option 1` (recommended) before `Option 2` (manual). Each option is one fenced block with a `#` comment above every command, then one line that says what the reader now has.
- Precedence or lookup order: numbered list, highest first, each line `` `source` `` then its effect.
- Key concepts: one `###` per concept, one sentence that defines it, then the smallest real example (front matter, a five-line file, one command).
- Limits as numbers: "keep under 10 enabled per project", never "too many". Put them in a notes section near the end.
- Customization: tell readers what to keep, change and remove; never imply that one setup fits all.
- Contributing: a short list of wanted contribution kinds, then the link to `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Horizontal rules (`---`) only between top-level sections of a README longer than ~150 lines.
- End with the license line. No star request, slogan or sign-off after it.
- Every command, path and count in the doc exists and is current; update it in the same change as the code.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/REPO/LAYOUT.md -->
---
id: conventions.repo.layout
---
## Repository layout
> Load when: creating a repo, adding top-level files or directories, or auditing a repo against the conventions.

| File | When | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | always | What it is, one-line install, usage, how it works (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`) |
| `LICENSE` | always | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LICENSE.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` (`@AGENTS.md`) | always | Working rules for coding agents (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/AGENTS-MD.md`) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | when kept | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CHANGELOG-MD.md` |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` | override of the org default | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CONTRIBUTING-MD.md`, `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SECURITY-MD.md`, `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CODE-OF-CONDUCT-MD.md` |
| `.github/CODEOWNERS` | ≥ 2 maintainers | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CODEOWNERS.md` |
| `.mcp.json` | shared MCP servers | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/MCP-JSON.md` |
| `DESIGN.md` | new projects | The owner's brief (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/DESIGN-MD.md`) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` | DB, daemon or plugin system | Binding contract per major version |
| `PKGBUILD`, `flake.nix` | anything installable | `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`, `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md` |
| CI workflow | always | Build the package and run tests on every PR (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`) |

- Directories by job: source (`cmd/`, `internal/`, `src/`), `scripts/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `completions/`; packaging at the root or in a packaging subdirectory.
- One entry point: one command with subcommands, not a pile of loose scripts.
- Features are files: modules, plugins, drivers and addons live in their own directory and can be added, toggled and removed without touching the core.
- Never commit: secrets, machine-local overrides (`*.local.*`), build output, large data or model artefacts. Gitignore them.
- Superseded code moves to a legacy directory or into git history; never leave dead copies next to live ones.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/REPO/STE100PP.md -->
---
id: conventions.repo.ste100pp
locales: pl=AGENTS/skills/ste100pp/references/PL.md
---
## STE100++ controlled writing
> Load when: writing or reviewing docs prose, procedures, help text, error messages, tool descriptions or agent prompts.

This standard is inspired by ASD-STE100 and is not certified. It does not reproduce the ASD dictionary. Full mode, scope table and self-check: `AGENTS/skills/ste100pp/SKILL.md`. Locale companions, written natively per language (first: `pl`): `AGENTS/skills/ste100pp/references/PL.md`. Scope: prose. Rule one-liners, code, tables of identifiers and quoted text are exempt.

- Answer or result in the first sentence. No preamble, no restated question.
- One idea per sentence. One action per procedure step, then its expected result.
- Active voice with a named actor. Passive only when the actor is unknown or irrelevant.
- Condition before command: "If the build fails, read the log." Warning: command first, then the risk.
- No semicolons in prose. Write two sentences.
- One word, one meaning: one term per concept in a file. New concept terms are defined once at first use.
- Verbs, not nominalizations: "check", not "perform a check".
- Sentence length: ≤ 20 words in procedures, ≤ 25 in explanations, 30 hard cap.
- Keep real uncertainty (may, might) with one hedge. Delete stacked hedges and claim words (`CONVENTIONS/REPO/WRITING.md`).
- Keep articles, subjects and "that". Short is not telegraphic.
- Numbers as digits with units (`30 s`, `2 GiB`), dates ISO 8601, one name per command or file, in backticks.
- Error messages: what happened, the cause if known, the next action. No apology, no blame.
- Never change code, commands, identifiers, quoted errors, numbers or the strength of a hedge to fit a rule.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/REPO/WRITING.md -->
---
id: conventions.repo.writing
---
## Writing & voice
> Load when: writing docs, help text, error messages, commit messages, or community and lore text.

- English for everything structural: code, identifiers, comments, docs, config keys, commits, logs.
- Use the profile's cultural language for `README-<locale>.md`, community posts and lore. One language per file.
- Never translate machine-parsed identifiers (commands, config keys, schema fields, event names).
- Docs voice: plain, honest, specific, second person. Name limits and risks. No filler adjectives ("modern", "clean", "powerful", "seamless") and no claim words ("production-ready", "battle-tested", "comprehensive"): state the count, test or platform instead. Profile and examples: `AGENTS/PROMPT/DOCS-VOICE.md`.
- No bold lead-ins on list items; put the identifier in backticks.
- Humor (™, memes, lore) lives in profiles, banners and lore docs; never in specs, error messages or identifiers.
- `™` and other marks never appear in identifiers, package names or config.
- Dense: cut every word that does not change the meaning. Rules are imperative one-liners.
- Prose structure (sentences, procedures, errors, hedges): `CONVENTIONS/REPO/STE100PP.md`.

<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/CONVENTIONS-FORMAT.md -->
---
id: conventions.specs.original.format-1.0
---
## Conventions Format 1.0
> Load when: implementing, validating, or changing the Conventions Format 1.0 document contract.

**Format 1.0** · [spec landing page](https://szmelc-inc.github.io/CONVENTIONS.md/SPEC/) · [schema set](https://szmelc-inc.github.io/CONVENTIONS.md/SPEC/schemas/)

### Status and language

This document defines Conventions Format 1.0, a repository-independent format for collections of Markdown instruction rules, indexes, profiles, and overlays. The format version describes this document contract. A repository's release version describes that repository's releases and is independent of the format version.

Interpret the key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **REQUIRED**, **SHALL**, **SHALL NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT**, **RECOMMENDED**, **NOT RECOMMENDED**, **MAY**, and **OPTIONAL** as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119 and RFC 8174). This meaning applies only when each term appears in uppercase.

An implementation conforms to version 1.0 when it follows all applicable MUST and MUST NOT requirements in this document. SHOULD-level recommendations permit a documented, reasoned exception. This document does not require a particular programming language, parser library, or host agent.

### Format versioning

Every format manifest or index that declares a format version MUST use `format_version: "1.0"` for this version. A format version MUST NOT be inferred from a repository version, release tag, directory name, or schema version. A repository MAY contain rules in this format without publishing a manifest. In that case its documentation or distribution metadata declares the format version.

The format version follows `MAJOR.MINOR`. A major increment denotes an incompatible change to required parsing, data model, or interpretation. A minor increment denotes an additive change that a 1.0 reader can safely ignore. A correction that does not change conforming input or interpretation MAY be published without changing the format version. Readers MUST reject an unsupported major version. Readers of 1.0 MAY ignore unknown optional fields. They MUST NOT reinterpret a known field based on the repository's release version.

Rule `id` values identify rules, not releases or file locations. An ID MUST be unique within a collection, MUST remain unchanged when the rule is moved or retitled, and MUST NOT be reused after removal. The format does not prescribe a globally unique namespace across unrelated repositories.

### Rule files

A rule is a UTF-8 Markdown file with a first-level heading, a `Load when` line, and zero or one YAML front matter block. A rule file MUST begin either with `# ` or with a front matter delimiter at the start of the file. If present, the front matter MUST be the first block and MUST close before the Markdown body. After front matter, the first nonblank content line MUST be `# <title>` and the next nonblank line MUST be `> Load when: <expression>`.

The title and trigger line MUST each occupy one physical line. The title MUST be non-empty. The trigger expression MUST be non-empty. A rule MUST have a stable `id` in front matter when it is indexed as stable or experimental. A collection MUST reject duplicate IDs.

Front matter is a format convention layered over YAML. YAML itself does not define Markdown front matter. The opening and closing delimiters are lines containing exactly three ASCII hyphen-minus characters (`---`), with no surrounding whitespace. The enclosed content MUST parse as exactly one YAML mapping. It MUST use the YAML 1.2.2 core schema as restricted below. Duplicate mapping keys, aliases, anchors, explicit tags, merge keys, multiple YAML documents, and non-JSON values (including timestamps, binary values, and non-finite numbers) are invalid. Scalars MUST be interpreted as strings, booleans, null, or finite JSON numbers. Implementations MUST NOT apply YAML 1.1 implicit boolean or date coercions.

The JSON Schema at `SPEC/schemas/front-matter.schema.json` validates the decoded mapping. It does not parse YAML or validate Markdown framing. A conforming validator MUST perform both steps.

The following keys are defined:

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Stable rule identifier; REQUIRED for indexed stable and experimental rules. |
| `status` | string | Optional lifecycle label: `stable`, `experimental`, or `legacy`. Directory or collection policy MAY define status when omitted. |
| `scope` | array of strings | Optional repository-relative path globs to which the rule applies. |
| `tools` | array of strings | Optional host or tool identifiers for which the rule is intended. These labels do not guarantee host support. |
| `tags` | array of strings | Optional topic labels. |
| `since` | string | Optional format or collection release identifier that introduced the rule. It is informational and MUST NOT change parsing. |
| `supersedes` | array of strings | Optional IDs of rules this rule replaces. This records a relationship; it does not itself delete or disable those rules. |
| `locales` | string | Optional space-separated `<language-tag>=<path>` companion mappings. English stays canonical; each path is relative to the collection root and points to a companion document outside the indexed rule tree. |

An ID MUST match `[a-z0-9]+([.-][a-z0-9]+)*`. `scope`, `tools`, `tags`, and `supersedes` MUST contain only non-empty strings and MUST NOT contain duplicate values. Unknown front matter keys are extensions: a 1.0 reader MUST preserve or ignore them without assigning meaning. Producers SHOULD use a reverse-domain or repository-qualified prefix for extension keys to reduce collisions.

The `locales` value contains space-separated `tag=path` pairs. For example, use `locales: pl=translations/RULE-PL.md`. Tags MUST be valid BCP 47 language tags and unique after case-insensitive comparison. Paths MUST be safe collection-relative paths that exist. A path MUST NOT point to the canonical English rule. The canonical rule remains the source for IDs, triggers, status and scope. A consumer MAY show a language selector when companions exist. Missing languages MUST fall back to English. Companion files are not separate rules. They MUST NOT be indexed or included in an all-rules bundle.

### Schemas and conformance

The normative schemas are published under the stable site path `SPEC/schemas/`. A schema URL ending in `index-v2.schema.json` validates the index object. `front-matter.schema.json` validates a parsed rule metadata mapping. `profile.schema.json` validates the JSON profile interchange object. Source profiles MAY use another serialization, such as TOML. They MUST normalize to that object before validation. `compat-registry.schema.json` validates the compatibility registry interchange object and the `compatible` records embedded in an index. Schema URLs are immutable within a format major version. A breaking schema change requires a new major-version directory and identifier.

Schemas validate data shape, not all format semantics. A conforming implementation MUST additionally check unique rule IDs and paths, references to existing files, front-matter delimiters, heading/trigger order, path glob safety, and valid trigger syntax. The reference suite in `SPEC/tests/` includes both valid and invalid inputs. A validator MUST reject every invalid fixture and accept every valid fixture. Implementations SHOULD add fixtures for edge cases they discover.

### Interoperability and native adapters

An adapter compiles each rule independently and retains its stable `id`, title, trigger, optional scope and body. It MUST NOT silently turn every lazy rule into an always-on instruction. Where a host has no native lazy selector, the adapter MUST state that limitation and emit an on-demand reference or a clearly labelled one-shot bundle. The supported mappings and limits are recorded in `SPEC/INTEROP.md`.

Each generated output MUST include enough source information to trace it to the originating rule. An implementation MUST escape metadata for the target format and MUST treat the Markdown body as data, not as a template. It MUST NOT evaluate shell syntax or interpolate rule content into commands.

### Change process

Format changes begin as a GitHub Discussion tagged RFC. An accepted proposal is published under `CONVENTIONS/EXPERIMENTAL/` with an owner, rationale, compatibility notes and a decision record under `SPEC/decisions/`. After review and conformance fixtures, a proposal MAY move to stable. The decision record states accepted alternatives and migration impact. A change to the meaning of a 1.0 field is prohibited. Additive optional fields MAY be standardized as a compatible revision. Breaking semantics require Format 2.0.

### License

The specification prose is licensed under MIT, the same license as this repository. Implementations remain free to use any license. Reusers SHOULD preserve the copyright and license notice when copying prose.

#### Path glob syntax

All paths and patterns use `/` as the separator, regardless of the host operating system. A pattern is relative to the collection root, MUST NOT begin with `/`, and MUST NOT contain a `..` path segment. Matching is case-sensitive and is performed against a normalized relative path with `.` segments removed. Backslash is an ordinary character and MUST NOT be treated as a separator or escape.

The glob operators are `*`, `?`, bracket classes, and `**`. `*` matches zero or more characters other than `/`. `?` matches one character other than `/`. Bracket classes such as `[abc]` or `[a-z]` match one character other than `/`. `**` matches zero or more characters including `/` wherever it appears. A bracket class MUST be closed and non-empty. An initial `!` negates the class. All other characters match themselves. Implementations MUST apply these rules to `scope` patterns and `glob` trigger atoms.

#### Trigger expression

The text after `> Load when:` is a trigger expression. Its purpose is to let a reader decide whether to load a rule. The expression uses the following ABNF (RFC 5234). Literal names are case-sensitive. The payload of `keyword` and `task` is case-insensitive:

```abnf
expression = ws atom *(ws ("AND" / "OR") ws atom) ws
atom       = keyword / glob / task / text
keyword    = "keyword(" quoted ")"
glob       = "glob(" quoted ")"
task       = "task(" quoted ")"
text       = "text(" quoted ")"
quoted     = DQUOTE 1*(qchar / escape) DQUOTE
qchar      = %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E / UTF8-OCTET
escape     = %x5C (DQUOTE / %x5C)
ws         = *(SP / HTAB)
DQUOTE     = %x22
SP         = %x20
HTAB       = %x09
UTF8-OCTET = %x80-FF
```

The ABNF is applied to UTF-8 octets. The complete trigger line MUST also be valid UTF-8. `UTF8-OCTET` does not by itself validate a multibyte sequence.

`AND` binds more tightly than `OR`. Parentheses and implicit operators are not part of version 1.0. A `keyword` atom matches a whole case-insensitive token in the user's task text. A `task` atom matches a whole case-insensitive task-class token supplied by the caller. Examples include `build`, `review`, and `documentation`. The format does not prescribe a universal task-class vocabulary. A `glob` atom matches a repository-relative path under the path-glob rules above. It is true if it matches any path in the task context. A `text` atom is descriptive natural-language guidance evaluated by the consuming agent. It has no deterministic string-matching algorithm. An expression is a candidate to load when it evaluates true. A consumer that cannot evaluate one or more atom types MAY use the complete trigger line as a natural-language hint. It MUST NOT claim deterministic matching for those atoms.

For backward compatibility with existing collections, version 1.0 readers MAY accept a non-empty trigger line that is not a valid expression as a legacy natural-language trigger. Producers of new 1.0 rule files SHOULD use the explicit atom syntax. Legacy trigger lines are hints only and do not have deterministic matching semantics.

### Cores and maps

A core is a named collection of rules and supporting documents. A core map is a Markdown file that lists paths, short descriptions, and load triggers. Map generation and directory layout are repository choices. This format does not require a particular build script.

When a collection provides `INDEX.md`, it MUST use UTF-8 Markdown. It SHOULD explain how to read the index. It SHOULD then list always-loaded entry points, cores, stable rules, skills, experimental material, and legacy material as applicable. Each listed path MUST be relative to the collection root and MUST identify one entry. An index MUST distinguish experimental entries from stable rules and MUST mark legacy entries as archival. Human-readable indexes MAY omit fields that are present in `index.json`.

Generated maps and indexes SHOULD carry a notice identifying them as generated and pointing to their authoritative sources. Consumers MUST treat such generated files as read-only outputs when source files are available.

### `index.json` version 2

`index.json` is a UTF-8 JSON object. A version 2 index MUST include a `$schema` string, `format_version`, `name`, `repo`, `entries`, `compatible_disclaimer`, and `compatible`. `format_version` MUST be `"1.0"`. `$schema` identifies the schema for this JSON instance. It does not declare the Conventions format version. `name` is the collection's short name. `repo` is its canonical repository URI.

`entries` is an ordered array. Every entry MUST include `path`, `title`, `load_when`, `status`, and `kind`. `path` is a unique normalized relative path with `/` separators and no `.` or `..` segments. `title` and `load_when` are non-empty strings. `status` is `always`, `stable`, `experimental`, or `legacy`. `kind` is `global`, `core`, `skill`, `rule`, or `archive`. A `rule` entry MUST include its front matter `id`. Other entry kinds MAY include `id` when the collection defines its meaning. An entry MAY include `origin` (`third-party` or `original`) and `compat`, an array of compatibility-record IDs.

`compatible_disclaimer` is a string. `compatible` is an ordered array of compatibility records. Each record MUST contain `id`, `name`, `kind`, `description`, `version`, `added`, `updated`, `spec`, and `links`. `kind` is `format`, `spec`, `platform`, `tool`, `language`, or `stack`. `spec` is an array of collection-relative rule paths. `links` is an object with optional URI keys: `homepage`, `repo`, `docs`, and `community`. `icon` MAY be a collection-relative asset path. Record IDs MUST be unique. Dates in `added` and `updated` MUST use the full-date form `YYYY-MM-DD`.

JSON object member order is insignificant. Readers MUST preserve array order. A 1.0 reader MAY ignore unknown object members. JSON strings MUST use UTF-8 and valid JSON escaping. A consumer MUST reject malformed JSON and invalid required values. The schemas and reference validator are published in `SPEC/`.

### Profiles and overlays

A profile supplies collection-specific values such as project name, URLs, paths, and display settings. Profiles are data, not executable instructions. A profile's values MUST NOT alter the meaning of format fields or the trigger grammar. A profile MAY define additional string-valued variables for template rendering.

An overlay applies a bounded set of overrides to a selected profile. The 1.0 TOML overlay model has `[overrides]` with optional `disable = ["<rule-id>", ...]`. It MAY also have `[overrides.set]` with string-valued `profile.<key> = "<value>"` entries. An overlay MUST disable rules by stable ID, never by path. It MUST NOT introduce or rewrite rule content. A collection MAY define precedence. When it supports common layers, use this order: base profile, organization profile, team overlay, project overlay, then user overlay. Later string assignments replace earlier values. Disabled IDs are cumulative. A later overlay cannot re-enable a disabled rule. A renderer MUST reject IDs that do not exist in the selected collection.

The format does not prescribe how a host discovers, activates, combines, or prioritizes profiles or overlays. A collection MUST document any precedence beyond these rules.

### Host behavior and interoperability boundary

The format defines portable document content and selectors. It does not guarantee that an agent host discovers files or follows nested directories. A host may ignore a glob field, fail to activate a rule on demand, or resolve conflicts differently. A host MAY require an adapter that translates the format into its native instruction mechanism. Adapters MUST preserve rule meaning to the extent the target host can express it. They SHOULD report unsupported selectors instead of presenting them as guaranteed behavior.

Automatic discovery paths, context-size limits, instruction precedence, skills installation, adapter output, and runtime rule selection are out of scope. A collection's documentation MUST state host-specific behavior it relies on.

### Prose license

The normative prose uses the repository's MIT License, the same license as the surrounding project. A collection that adopts this format MAY choose another license for its own prose. Conformance does not transfer ownership or licensing of rule content.

### References

- [RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119.html)
- [RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174.html)
- [RFC 5234: Augmented BNF for Syntax Specifications](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5234.html)
- [YAML 1.2.2 Specification](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/)
- [JSON Schema Draft 2020-12](https://json-schema.org/specification)
- [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/)

id: conventions.specs.original.core-maps
---
## Core maps
> Load when: organising a doc tree into cores, adding a core or category, or editing a core README.

- Core = UPPERCASE directory `X/` + guide `X/README.md` + generated root map `X.md`.
- `X/README.md`: line 1 `# Title`, line 2 `> Load when: <trigger>`, then what the core holds and a table of its categories.
- Root map `X.md`: generated: title, trigger, link to the guide, then `| Path | What | Load when |` rows from each file's header. Never hand-edit.
- A hand-written root file keeps its map between `<!-- map:begin -->` and `<!-- map:end -->`; only that block is generated.
- Nested categories repeat the pattern; `X/<SUB>/README.md` is optional, only when a category needs more than its table row.
- Every category directory has a row in its core guide's table.
- Any project may adopt it for a doc tree; the build script generates maps and indexes (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/INDEX-MD.md`).
- A repository defines its own cores and root maps; profile identity content belongs in the selected profile.

<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/DESIGN-MD.md -->
---
id: conventions.specs.original.design-md
---
## Design docs & agent briefs
> Load when: starting a project, writing a brief for a coding agent, or changing a project's architecture.

| File | Written by | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `DESIGN.md` | Owner, own words | Raw intent: what, for whom, why; constraints; nice-to-haves marked as such. Agents never rewrite it. |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` | Agent + owner | Binding contract for major version N: paths, config, CLI, storage, tests. |
| `docs/<NAME>-SPEC.md` | Agent + owner | Contract between a runtime and its extensions (addons, plugins, drivers). |
| `<SOURCE>.md` | Human | External source document an implementation follows. |

- Read `DESIGN.md` and the current architecture contract before changing anything.
- A change that deviates from the contract updates the contract in the same commit.
- Briefs: ordered phases, each with a literal acceptance criterion; a phase starts only when the previous one passes; report after each.
- Build a thin working vertical slice first, never broad stubs.
- List fixed tech decisions with a one-line reason each, and one anchor example (config, CLI session) the implementation must match.
- Ambiguity → the simplest option that satisfies the brief, assumption stated inline, keep going.
- "Reproducible" means repeatable from the same inputs unless bit-for-bit is stated.

id: conventions.specs.original.index-md
---
## Lazy-load indexes
> Load when: generating, reading or changing INDEX.md, index.json or an all-in-one rule bundle.

- Generated by the build script from file headers (first content line is the title, followed by `> Load when:`); stable and experimental rule IDs come from YAML front matter. The generated `INDEX.md` carries a "generated, do not edit" comment. Never hand-edit; the build's `--check` mode fails CI when stale.
- `INDEX.md`: `# Index`, a read-once instruction, then `| File | Load when |` tables per section: Always on, Cores, Rules, Skills, Experimental (opt-in only), Legacy (title only).
- `index.json`: `name`, `repo`, `entries[]` with `path`, `title`, `load_when`, `status` (`always|stable|experimental|legacy`), `kind` (`global|core|skill|rule|archive`), stable `id` for rules, optional `origin` (`third-party|original`, from the path) and `compat` (registry ids citing the file); `compatible_disclaimer` and `compatible[]` from `META/compat/registry.toml`; schema `META/schema/index.schema.json`.
- Bundle (`CONVENTIONS.md`): map of the rule tree, then every stable rule inlined, headings demoted one level, each after a `<!-- source: <path> -->` marker. For tools that cannot lazy-load; never loaded together with the index.
- Agents read `INDEX.md` once per session, then only files whose trigger matches; never bulk-read, never `@import` rule files into always-on instructions.
- Web index of the same entries: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LLMS-TXT.md`. Maps per core: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/CORE-MAPS.md`.
